overview: This Senate resolution celebrates the 52nd annual National Catholic Schools Week, held January 25 to 31, 2026, and organized by the National Catholic Educational Association and the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops. It describes Catholic elementary and high schools as serving about 1.7 million students, including many from minority and non-Catholic families, and cites high graduation and college attendance rates reported by the education association. The resolution supports the week's goals and praises the schools' students, parents, and teachers. The Senate agreed to it on January 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes schools that educate a large and diverse group of students and play an important role in many communities.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, and some may question the Senate singling out schools of one religious tradition for praise.
